subject: Exception intake + comms plan for model transition (clarify ownership & SLAs)
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-18T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Exception intake + comms plan for model transition (clarify ownership & SLAs)

Hi team,

We have an Acme request that surfaced this morning: they need an explicit exception path and comms cadence for the upcoming model transition (variant consolidation planned for November). They asked whether we can provide a one-week canary, what the rollback SLA is, and whether audit logs and token-level cost breakdowns will be visible to their platform team during the window.

As a cross-functional ask I want to:
- Lock ownership for exception intake (who triages and signs off)
- Define a short comms timeline to customers on exceptions (what we tell them, and when)
- Surface any hard constraints (capacity, rollout windows, billing implications) that would block a canary or extend the approval timeline

I attached a filled exception_form_v2.xlsx and a draft proposed-comm-timeline.md for starter language. Please respond with:
1) Who is the owner for intake & approval (product / infra / CS)?
2) Whether a one-week canary is feasible; if not, what minimal window can we commit to?
3) Any contractual or billing flags (Neha) that would prevent us from offering an exception for Acme.

Irene
Irene Choi
Product Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachments: exception_form_v2.xlsx, proposed-comm-timeline.md

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-18T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Exception intake + comms plan for model transition (clarify ownership & SLAs)

Thanks Irene — catching this early is helpful. My initial thoughts:
- Product should own the intake and decision classification (critical vs non-critical). We can then hand off to Infra for rollout constraints.
- For Acme specifically I can own the comm copy and coordinate with CS to make sure messaging aligns with contract.
- A one-week canary is acceptable as a target but depends on infra capacity and whether we need a variant fallback to maintain SLA. If infra says it's risky, we propose 3-day canary + contingency fallback.

Action items for me: prepare classification rubric and sample comms (by EOD).

Marissa

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-18T11:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Exception intake + comms plan for model transition (clarify ownership & SLAs)

Short summary from infra perspective:
- Capacity: we can support a one-week canary if we schedule a reserved slot (we'd need a day-of notice to carve GPU pool and ensure KV cache warmup). No more than two simultaneous customer canaries during a week.
- Rollback SLA: we can guarantee rollback within 2 business hours provided the request is submitted with the rollback trigger (error threshold / latency delta) and we keep the KV caches intact. Immediate rollback (under 30m) is risky during peak hours.
- Observability: we can expose token-level latency and request/response logs for the canary to Acme's platform team; cost breakdown exposure requires a short billing workstream (Neha).

Attachments: runbook excerpt (refer to exception_form_v2.xlsx sheet 'infra-runbook').

Ben
Head of Infra Operations

On 2026-10-18, Marissa Cole wrote:
> My initial thoughts: Product should own the intake and decision classification...

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-18T13:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Exception intake + comms plan for model transition (clarify ownership & SLAs)

Quick billing/contract note:
- Acme's current contract (SaaS - Enterprise Tier) allows for up to two "special maintenance windows" per 12 months without additional fees; more than that requires an amendment. We need to confirm whether this canary counts as a maintenance window.
- If Acme requests token-level cost reporting for the canary, we need a signed amendment for extended reporting/audit access (privacy + billing disclosures).

Irene — can you loop Acme's platform contact (Sarah) so we can get explicit acceptance on a canary counting as a maintenance window?

Neha
Senior Account Executive, Sales

On 2026-10-18, Ben Carter wrote:
> Short summary from infra perspective: Capacity: we can support a one-week canary if we schedule a reserved slot...

From: Sarah Jones <sarah.jones@acme.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: platform-team@acme.com
Date: 2026-10-18T15:31:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Exception intake + comms plan for model transition (clarify ownership & SLAs)

Thanks Neha / Irene — confirming Acme's position:
- We are OK with the canary being treated as a maintenance window (one per transition).
- We'd prefer a one-week window but can accept a 3-day canary if it keeps risk lower.
- We need read-access to request/response logs during the window and a view into token-level latency/costs for the canary only. We are comfortable signing a short amendment for the billing visibility piece.

Two quick asks from our team:
1) Can we get the proposed comm copy in advance (we'll share a short internal notice to our platform users)?
2) Will rollback be automated or manual (we prefer automated rollback to minimize customer impact)?

Sarah Jones
Platform Lead, Acme Corp

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Sarah Jones <sarah.jones@acme.com>
Date: 2026-10-19T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Exception intake + comms plan for model transition (clarify ownership & SLAs)

Thanks all — quick consolidation and next steps:
- Ownership: Product (Marissa) owns intake and comms; Infra (Ben) owns rollout and rollback mechanics; Sales (Neha) owns contracting for amendments.
- Canary window: target = 7 days. Backup plan = 3-day canary + automatic variant fallback. Ben: schedule reserved slot and confirm latest start date by Friday.
- Rollback: Infra to implement an automated rollback trigger (2-hour SLA for manual fallback). Ben, please confirm automation feasibility and list required observability hooks.
- Billing: Neha to draft amendment language for token-level reporting; Sarah to confirm sign-off.
- Comms: Marissa to share comm copy and internal classification rubric (Marissa to send EOD tomorrow). I will schedule a 30-min cross-functional sync for Thursday to lock timelines.

Related links: https://docs.google.com/document/d/comm-plan, https://hubspot.example.com/deal/12345

Irene
Product Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachments: proposed-comm-timeline.md
